Notes

麻痹

麻痹 literally refers to numbness or paralysis, but this construction uses its sound as a stand-in for a coarse insult. Reading it medically would miss the opening’s aggressive invitation to get up and party.

  • Genius community lyric text
纸上谈兵

Literally discussing military strategy on paper. The idiom criticizes abstract talk with no practical ability behind it; the following official-sounding declarations become examples.

  • Genius community lyric text
强烈谴责

“Strongly condemn” and the following “solemnly protest” are formulas used in official diplomatic statements. Putting them after flooding a social feed makes the online outburst sound comically state-like. The cited statement demonstrates the register; the lyric does not name its particular dispute.

  • Genius community lyric text
  • Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs: example of both formulas
骗鬼呢

Literally “are you fooling ghosts?”—a dismissive way of saying nobody would believe this. The repeated 鬼 also connects the chorus to the ghosts and devils in the guest verse.

  • Genius community lyric text
城市套路多我回农村

This recalls the circulated saying 城市套路深，我要回农村: the city’s tricks run deep, so I’m returning to the countryside. A 2016 Xinhua report already described it as a popular phrase. Chun immediately punctures the escape fantasy with the muddy road’s holes and traps.

  • Genius community lyric text
  • Xinhua report on the circulated phrase, via People’s Daily
坑

坑 can be a literal pit or a figurative trap or scam. Returning to muddy rural roads does not escape the city’s 套路, its tricks and schemes.

  • Genius community lyric text
大楼建基层

The community text prints 建基层, roughly “build the base level.” This translation reads it as a likely transcription of 建几层, “build how many floors”: 几层 and 基层 sound very similar. That is an editorial reading, not an audio-verified correction; the printed Chinese is preserved. The later line beginning 我祈求 also has an abrupt pronoun shift, retained in the English.

  • Genius community lyric text
人心隔肚皮

Literally, the heart is separated from view by the belly’s skin. The saying means someone’s intentions cannot be known from the outside. Pairing it with acting tough online questions the reliability of the persona on display.

  • Genius community lyric text
笨鸟先飞

This proverb says that a less gifted person can compensate by starting earlier and working harder. The added image of being covered in excrement abruptly soils the familiar encouragement; the slow bird is neither elegant nor triumphant.

  • Genius community lyric text
娘子

娘子 is an older form of address for a woman or wife. Here it gives the repeated romantic call a theatrical, old-fashioned flavor amid the much rougher talk about money, ambition, and confrontation.

  • Genius community lyric text
算命老师

老师 can be an honorific for a practitioner, not only a schoolteacher. The fortune-teller’s call is later answered by 改命, changing fate, and the boast that Chun’s progress did not depend on a master. The verse sets prediction against making one’s own way.

  • Genius community lyric text
范冰冰

Fan Bingbing is a Chinese actor and producer. Calling the woman “my Fan Bingbing” borrows a recognizable screen-star image as a personal comparison; it does not identify the woman as the celebrity herself.

  • Genius community lyric text
  • San Sebastián Festival: Fan Bingbing biography
老子

老子 here is a swaggering, confrontational way of referring to oneself, roughly “your old man” used as “I.” It is not a reference to the philosopher Laozi. English distributes the aggression into “fucking” instead of translating the kinship term literally.

  • Genius community lyric text
老汉

老汉 can mean “Dad” in regional speech. Nearby, 打螺丝 literally means fastening screws and commonly evokes repetitive factory work; 黑中介 is an unscrupulous intermediary or broker.

  • Genius community lyric text
眼中钉

The Chinese idiom names a nail in the eye: someone so resented that one wants them removed. English’s familiar “thorn in your side” transfers the meaning but softens the original location, which belongs to this verse’s unusually bodily language.

  • Genius community lyric text
刀人

刀 (“knife”) is used as a verb here, conveying stabbing or attacking someone with a knife. The translation keeps the violent image rather than treating it as a neutral argument.

  • Genius community lyric text
